── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Strong first week: three runs done, no pain, heart rate under control. …
Answers: No, please do not run every day yet. Your body is brand new to this, and the gap days are where the fitness actually gets built.
Safety flag: Calf tightness is normal early on
Next week:
Mon: easy, 2.5 km walk-run, 1 min run / 90 sec walk, keep heart rate under 150. Repeats…
Tue: other, 20 – 30 min easy dog walk. Keeps the legs moving and helps the calves settle.
Wed: easy, 2.5 km walk-run, same 1 min run / 90 sec walk intervals, conversational…
Thu: other, 20 – 30 min easy walk. Light aerobic day between runs.
Fri: rest. Sets up a fresher Saturday long one.
Sat: long, 3.0 km walk-run, 1 min run / 90 sec walk, slow and steady. The week's…
Sun: other, 30 – 40 min easy walk. Recovery day on your feet, no running.
